messages:
Sam: Quick heads-up — noticed a p95 spike on canary around 21:12. Telemetry points to the new congestion-aware slen sampler moving a bunch of requests into the long-context path.
Nina: Can you paste the traces? wondering if KV warmup is the culprit or just poor kernel pick for mid-lengths.
Sam: Paste of a couple lines from trace: 
```
[2026-03-17T21:12:03Z] gpu0 trace kernel_pick=matmul_v3 seq_len=384 path=decode batch=1 p50=18ms p95=60ms
[2026-03-17T21:12:03Z] gpu0 trace kernel_pick=matmul_v2 seq_len=1024 path=prefill batch=4 p50=22ms p95=95ms
```
Sam: Notice the matmul_v2 pick for 1024 in prefill — p95 is much higher than last week.
Aj: That sounds like the kernel-autotuner bumped v2 for 1k because of throughput regressions elsewhere. Did we change kernel scoring weights last deploy?
Devin: We did tweak the architecture penalty for Ampere because Hopper seemed to prefer fused kernels. Might be the autotuner misreading short-term noise as a trend.
Carlos: Also check KV hit rates. If cache_warmup=false then prefill for midseq gets heavier because we re-stream KV.
Sam: KV hit for the affected traces looks ~52% vs usual ~78%. So worse warmup.
Nina: Oof. Two vectors: sampler moved midseq into long path + cache miss amplifies cost. Combined effect explains spike.
Aj: Proposed short mitigation: lower the congestion sampler aggressiveness and force seqlen threshold for short path to 512 for canary. Quick config snippet: 
```
slen_sampler:
  mode: congestion_aware
  window: 60s
  max_short: 512
  aggressiveness: 0.4
  cache_warmup: true
```
Devin: Can we also add a temporary kernel-fallback rule: if seq_len in [256,768] and p95 > 2x baseline route to short-kernel-v4? We can collect telemetry for 1h.
Carlos: I can flip a conditional route in canary. Command I plan to run: 
```
/deploy route set --canary --cond "slen<512" --path "short-kernel-v4" --note "temp mitigate sampler misroute"
```
infra-bot: Rolling canary route change: job=route-update env=canary status=queued by Carlos
perf-bot: Alert: canary latency delta for model=text-phi v2 -> p95 +28% over 5m window (slen window 300-900)
Sam: Let's throttle the sampler, flip Carlos' route, and re-evaluate KV hit warmup (add extra prefill caching for 60s). Who's owning?
Carlos: I'll run the route flip in 5m and watch telemetry for 30m.
Devin: I'll revert the recent kernel scoring change if we still see regression after the route flip.
Nina: I'll investigate why cache_warmup dipped — looking at prefix cache eviction logs now.
Aj: Also logging experiment: sample 1% of requests and force them through the alt path to gather microbenchmarks (no user impact). Add flag: sampling_override=exp_slen_probe.
Sam: Cool. Action items: Carlos route flip, Nina cache investigation, Devin standby to revert kernel score, Aj will add sampling probe, Sam will coordinate metrics dashboard updates.
Carlos: Done — flip applied, infra-bot shows success.
infra-bot: route-update completed: job=route-update env=canary status=success by Carlos
perf-bot: Telemetry update: p95 in window decreased to +6% after route flip and sampler throttle. Continuing to monitor. :thumbsup:
Nina: Found a spike in eviction churn — looks like our adaptive cache window shrank due to memory pressure on that host group. Raising cache window back to 120s should help.
Devin: Good. If we still see anomalies after cache window restore we'll roll back the scoring tweak.
Sam: Thanks all. We'll keep the canary for 2 hours and then decide whether to push the scoring rollback to staging. If you collect any additional traces drop them here.
Aj: Dropping a small script to pull matching traces for later analysis: 
```
# query traces where kernel_pick in (matmul_v2,matmul_v3) and 256<=slen<=1024
python tools/query_traces.py --model text-phi --start -60m --filter "kernel_pick:matmul_v2,matmul_v3" > /tmp/slen_traces.json
```
Sam: Perfect. End of thread for now.
